summary: Computes per-point PCA-derived geometric signals (eigenvalues, planarity/linearity/scattering, normals, multi-K curvatures, Voronoi-area point weights, reliability, ternary RGB) for every LiDAR point in a building. Uses one kNN at K=32 with 3D spherical KDE weighting to compensate for anisotropic scan-line density, plus progressive K expansion (32→48→64→96→128) when the neighbourhood is physically elongated. Direct port of v2's unified tile-signals step that replaced three earlier steps (compute-tile-normals + compute-curvatures + compute-eigenvalues).

phases.name: Per-building gather + F32 cast
phases.description: For each building, gather global point indices from per-building-records, subtract the centroid from building-local-frames, and cast each (x,y,z) to Float32 then back to Float64. The F32 truncation matches v2's Float32Array positions byte-for-byte. The kd-tree from building-kd-trees is deserialised against the same F32-truncated values.

phases.name: kNN at K_STAGES[0]=32 + Voronoi point weight
phases.description: Query the pre-built per-building kd-tree for the 32 nearest neighbours. Emit ts-weights as π·d_k²/k from the k-th neighbour's squared distance (k=weight_k=8) — this is each point's local Voronoi cell area, used downstream by grow-refit-merge.

phases.name: Progressive K expansion (scan-line correction)
phases.description: Compute unweighted spatial linearity (λ1−λ2)/λ1 of the K=eigen_k neighbours. If it exceeds linearity_threshold, walk through K_STAGES = [32,48,64,96,128] re-fetching neighbours until linearity drops below threshold or K_MAX is reached. Once `expanded` trips, the curvature K-loop uses the full expanded neighbour set for slices ≥ K. Fixes LiDAR HD's 3-line/0.15m banding which produced 100% false linearity on flat surfaces.

phases.name: Spherical KDE direction weights
phases.description: Once the neighbour set is settled, build unit direction vectors from query to each neighbour. For each direction j, density_j = Σ_k exp(−chord²(j,k) / 2σ²), and weights = 1/density_j normalised to sum to 1. Equivalent to a von Mises-Fisher kernel on the sphere; compensates for angular clustering of scan lines in 3D regardless of surface tilt.

phases.name: Weighted PCA at each K slice
phases.description: For each ck in CURVATURE_KS = [8,16,32], run KDE-weighted PCA. Cardano closed-form eigensolver (pca.h port of v2 lib/geometry/pca.js). Emit ts-curv-k{ck} = λ3/(λ1+λ2+λ3) at every K. Smaller slices (k=8) stay at their own K — too local to benefit from expansion.

phases.name: Primary K outputs (K=eigen_k=16)
phases.description: On the eigen_k slice only: emit ts-eigen-l1/l2/l3, ts-planarity = (λ2−λ3)/λ1, ts-linearity = (λ1−λ2)/λ1, ts-scattering = λ3/λ1, ts-normals (smallest eigenvector, flipped along +up_axis), ts-eigen-rel = densityFactor × angularIsotropy, and ts-eigen-ternary (RGB packing of lin/plan/scat into 0..255). Degenerate points (<3 neighbours or λ1≈0) default to normal along +up_axis, scattering=1, blue ternary.

phases.name: ts-lidar-density emit
phases.description: After the per-building loop, compute tile-wide horizontal density = total_points / (Δh0·Δh1) on the two non-up axes (mirrors v2's lidar-density meta-artifact). Emitted as a public OPAQUE_JSON output; v7-grow-refit-merge consumes it for search-radius derivation.

parameters.name: eigenK
parameters.summary: Primary K for eigenvalues, normals, planarity/linearity/scattering, reliability and ternary.
parameters.rationale: K=16 is the sweet spot for LiDAR HD density (~20 pts/m²): large enough for stable PCA, small enough that ridges/edges remain locally distinguishable. Curvatures are also computed at K=8 and K=32 for multi-scale signals.

parameters.name: eigenMaxRadius
parameters.summary: Spatial radius cap used in the reliability density factor (count of K neighbours within this radius / K).
parameters.rationale: 1m balances 'this point has enough nearby support' against the largest expected K=128 reach on sparse fringes.

parameters.name: eigenAngularBandwidth
parameters.summary: Gaussian σ for 3D spherical KDE (π/8 ≈ 22.5°), applied to squared chord length between unit direction vectors.
parameters.rationale: σ = π/8 → vMF concentration κ ≈ 6.5. Resolves scan-line clustering (typical angular spread < 30°) without over-penalising moderate angular variation. See companion journal entry for the bandwidth derivation.

parameters.name: eigenSpatialLinearityThreshold
parameters.summary: Unweighted spatial linearity above which K is progressively expanded.
parameters.rationale: Scan-line bands at K=16 score 0.72–0.74; truly isotropic neighbourhoods score ~0.05. Threshold of 0.5 catches scan-line-elongated neighbourhoods while leaving genuinely planar/edge regions undisturbed. On dahouet 77% of points trigger expansion, 73% resolve at K=32.

history.note: Introduced together with the spatial-linearity trigger that replaced the earlier direction-scatter trigger (which missed 99.98% of scan-line cases).

parameters.name: weightK
parameters.summary: k for the Voronoi-area point weight w_i = π·d_k²/k. Piggybacks on the K_STAGES[0]=32 kNN already fetched.
parameters.rationale: k=8 gives a stable per-point inverse-density estimate without paying for a separate kNN. Output (ts-weights) is consumed downstream as an inverse local density signal.

parameters.name: upAxis
parameters.summary: Axis index (0=x, 1=y, 2=z) used to orient normals upward and to choose the two horizontal axes for tile-wide density.
parameters.rationale: v3 lidar-positions are in LAZ L93 frame (east, north, altitude) so altitude is axis 2. The pure-compute default in impl.c is 1 (v2 y-up) so the v2 bench harness gets byte-identical normals; the step wrapper overrides to 2 for v3 prod.

reads.name: lidar-positions
reads.description: Tile-wide F64 interleaved x,y,z (L93). Building-points are gathered from this via the global indices in per-building-records.

reads.name: per-building-records
reads.description: Per-building record (schema, n_verts, n_pts, footprint, then a Uint32 array of global inlier indices into lidar-positions).

reads.name: building-local-frames
reads.description: Per-building fixed-stride record: centroid_xyz (24B) + bbox_min_xyz (24B) + bbox_max_xyz (24B) in L93. Centroid is subtracted from gathered points to match v2's local-frame F32 precision.

reads.name: building-kd-trees
reads.description: Per-building pre-built kd-tree node array. Built over the same F32-truncated centroid-shifted positions this step gathers, so deserialisation is byte-consistent.

writes.name: ts-eigen-l1
writes.description: Largest PCA eigenvalue λ1 at K=eigen_k (Float32, per-building inline).

writes.name: ts-eigen-l2
writes.description: Middle PCA eigenvalue λ2 at K=eigen_k.

writes.name: ts-eigen-l3
writes.description: Smallest PCA eigenvalue λ3 at K=eigen_k.

writes.name: ts-curv-k8
writes.description: Scattering ratio λ3/(λ1+λ2+λ3) at K=8 (stays at k=8 even when expanded).

writes.name: ts-curv-k16
writes.description: Scattering ratio at K=16, uses expanded neighbourhood when K-expansion triggered.

writes.name: ts-curv-k32
writes.description: Scattering ratio at K=32, uses expanded neighbourhood when K-expansion triggered.

writes.name: ts-normals
writes.description: Float32 3·n_pts interleaved (nx,ny,nz). Smallest eigenvector of weighted covariance, flipped along +up_axis. Public visibility (consumed widely downstream).

writes.name: ts-eigen-rel
writes.description: Reliability = (neighbours within max_radius / K) × (1/Σw² / n). 1 = ideal isotropic, dense neighbourhood.

writes.name: ts-weights
writes.description: Per-point Voronoi cell area π·d_k²/k in m² (k=weightK=8 from K_STAGES[0]=32 kNN). Inverse-density signal used downstream.

writes.name: ts-eigen-ternary
writes.description: Uint8 3·n_pts — RGB packing of (linearity, planarity, scattering) clamped to 0..255 via JS-Math.round semantics.

writes.name: ts-lidar-density
writes.description: Tile-wide horizontal density (pts/m²) computed on the two non-up axes of lidar-positions. Single OPAQUE_JSON float (stringified %.17g).

v3_divergences.rationale: v2 runs PCA across the entire tile point cloud in one pass. v3 iterates per building, gathering only that building's points from lidar-positions via per-building-records and using the per-building kd-tree from build-building-kd-trees. Each kd-tree is shared across the v7 chain (Phase 5.2+ steps reuse the same artifact) instead of being a transient rebuilt by every downstream step.

v3_divergences.topic: kd-tree + centroid factored out into upstream steps
v3_divergences.rationale: v2's tile-signals built its own kd-tree internally as a transient artifact. v3 reads building-local-frames (centroid + bbox) and building-kd-trees, which are produced once by extract-buildings + build-building-kd-trees and shared across the v7 pipeline.

v3_divergences.topic: Up-axis is z (LAZ L93) in v3 prod, y in bench harness
v3_divergences.rationale: v3 lidar-positions are in L93 (east, north, altitude). The step wrapper sets up_axis=2 by default; v7_ts_params_default in impl.c keeps up_axis=1 so the standalone v7-tile-signals-bench CLI is byte-identical with v2 dumps. Up-axis only affects normal orientation and the horizontal-axis pair used for tile-wide density.

v2 emitted bare names like 'eigenvalue-l1' / 'planarity' / 'tile-normals' / 'point-weights'. v3 prefixes every v7 emit with the step tag (ts-*) so downstream resolution is unambiguous — needed because v3 has both a tile-wide path and per-building paths that would otherwise clash on the same artifact name.

Added in Phase 5 follow-up. v3 prod's extract-buildings reduces the working set per-building, so tile-wide density is no longer implicit. v7-grow-refit-merge and v7-derive-thresholds previously auto-computed density at point of use; centralising it here mirrors v2's lidar-density meta-artifact and lets downstream steps (and DERIV_LOG) read it instead of re-deriving.

ARRAY_INLINE writer now pads records to 8-byte alignment. Output bytes change vs. earlier v3 unpadded layout — step version bumped accordingly. Does not affect v2 parity since v2 doesn't share the on-disk container.

related.summary: Design journal: merged compute-tile-normals + compute-curvatures + compute-eigenvalues into the single tile-signals step. One kd-tree, one kNN at K_MAX=32, 17 artifacts, full cascade compatibility.
Why 3D spherical KDE replaces 2D circular KDE: 2D fails on slopes and walls, 3D vMF kernel with σ=π/8 correctly compensates scan-line anisotropy regardless of surface tilt.

Trigger for adaptive K expansion. Direction scatter (v3-v4) missed 99.98% of scan-line cases because 3-line bands still have angular diversity. Replaced with spatial linearity (λ1-λ2)/λ1 of neighbour positions — directly measures elongation. Progressive stages [32,48,64,96,128].
Closed-form Cardano eigensolver used by all the PCA paths in this step. Replaces earlier power iteration; O(1) per point, numerically stable.
Architectural context: in v2 the kd-tree was an explicit transient artifact emitted by tile-signals. v3 lifts it into the shared building-kd-trees artifact.
v2: initial unified tile-signals step — merges compute-tile-normals + compute-curvatures + compute-eigenvalues with 3D spherical KDE weighting.
v2: first attempt at dynamic K expansion using direction scatter dimensionality (later replaced — see 8da325b).
v2: spatial-linearity trigger replaces direction-scatter trigger. Progressive K stages [32,48,64,96,128].
v2: R2 global-index refactor — building-indices Uint32Array replaces building-points Array<{x,y,z}>. ptWeightsArr/normalsArr/curvature arrays become globally indexed (length = total tile points).
v3: Phase 5.0–5.1d — port v7-tile-signals to v3 (per-building processing, factored kd-tree + local-frames, ARRAY_INLINE 8-byte alignment).

v3: Phase 1 — eager rename pass. tile-signals artifacts gain ts-* prefix (ts-normals, ts-weights, ts-curv-k8/16/32, ts-linearity, ts-planarity, ts-scattering, ts-eigen-rel/l1/l2/l3, ts-eigen-ternary).
v3: add ts-lidar-density emit (step version 4). Mirrors v2 lidar-density; consumed by v7-grow-refit-merge and v7-derive-thresholds.
Phase 5 V7 port plan — 33-step → 26-main-path mapping, validation strategy, where v7-tile-signals fits in the pipeline.
